title: Why your body jolts just as you fall asleep ⚡
subject: sleep
description:
Does this happen to you every night? 👇

That sudden jolt or falling feeling as you drift off is called a hypnic jerk. Up to 70% of people get them, and scientists still debate why.

Sources: Oswald, Brain (1959) "Sudden bodily jerks on falling asleep", McGill Office for Science and Society ("What are Hypnic Jerks"), Sleep Foundation ("Hypnic Jerks")
tags: why do i jolt awake when falling asleep
why do we twitch in sleep

scenes.text: Your whole body jolts just as you fall asleep.
Often with a feeling of falling.
It's a hypnic jerk, described in a 1959 study. Up to 70% of people get them.
Caffeine, stress and poor sleep make them more common.
But here's the strange part. Scientists still aren't sure why.
One idea: as your muscles relax, your brain mistakes it for falling. Some think it's a reflex from ancestors who slept in trees. If so, your brain is trying to save you, every time
